Introduction/Background This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the requirements for the depot-level maintenance and repair of the NATO Seasparrow system components listed in Section 6. The objective of this SOW is to ensure the reliable and cost-effective repair of these components to CODE A condition, ready for issue, in accordance with the references located in Section 2. The work described herein is critical to maintaining the operational readiness and availability of the NATO Seasparrow system. 1.0 Scope The scope of this SOW encompasses all actions required to perform depot-level repair on the electronic components listed in Section 6. This includes, but is not limited to, receiving inspection, disassembly, cleaning, inspection, repair, replacement of parts, reassembly, testing, marking, and packaging according to the applicable Technical Repair Standard (TRS). In the absence of a TRS, the contractor may conduct the repair in accordance with locally generated procedures. In the case locally generated procedures are used, Final Acceptance Testing will be accomplished in accordance with the ap

m the BER DLR. 4.2.4 Quality Assurance and Record of Repair/TIDRR Quality Assurance checks shall be performed at all inspection hold points called out in the TRS by qualified quality assurance inspectors according to the TRS. In the absence of a TRS where the DLR is being serviced according to a locally generated procedure, The Contractor will, at a minimum, conduct a final inspection to verify proper reassembly, operation, finish, and required markings. When the DLR is packaged and ready for shipment, the Contractor will also conduct an inspection to assure proper packaging. Upon completion of repair and restoration of the DLR, the Traveler and Inspection/Discrepancy/Repair Report (TIDRR) shall serve as the official record of all examinations and tests conducted on the DLR. All discrepancies, recommended and corrective actions, test results, repair actions, as well as the data from examinations and inspections shall be recorded on a working copy of the TIDRR. It shall also verify the work performed during restoration/repair and remain with the DLR at all times. When completed, a copy of the TIDRR shall be retained by the overhaul and repair activity for review by the cognizant engineering agent and as a data source for repairables management program information requir
